newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power softer on storm fears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power softer on storm fears.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region softened Friday on concerns Hurricane Edouard would hit the U.S. East Coast this weekend, brokers and traders said.

"The thing that's driving people crazy is where is the hurricane going," said one regional trader, adding the temperatures for the eastern seaboard could vary as much as 10 degrees (Fahreneheit) next week depending on the storm's path.
According to the National Hurricane Center, Edouard lost strength, and turned north away from the Atlantic Coast, but the hurricane could backtrack over the weekend.
The uncertainty over the temperature outlook next week pressured weekend and next-week values lower in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool, brokers and traders said.
Peak electricity prices for the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend were quoted at $17.00-$17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from Thursday's $17.50-$18.00.
Weekend, off-peak prices in PJM were assessed in the $13.00 area, down from Thursday's range of $15.50-$16.50.
Next-week PJM electricity was quoted at $21.75-$22.50, down from $22.25-$22.75 on Thursday.

September PJM power for firm, peak delivery was pegged at $21.50-$22.00, compared with $21.50-$21.75 on Thursday. October PJM prices, under the same delivery conditions, were discussed at $20.25-$20.50, unchanged from Thursday's range.
Firm, peak electricity for November and December was flat from Thursday at $21.40-$21.55.
PJM firm, peak electricity for the fourth-quarter of 1996 was talked in the $22.25-$22.50, compared with Thursday's $22.30-$22.50.
PJM trading activity on Monday is expected to be extremely light due to the observance of Labor Day by most U.S. businesses.
